brief: The town has an evening door (spawnTapAgent), homers (spawnHomeAgent) and a night on the water that nobody watches: the night shot holds ONE person. Give the warm dry evening its own arrival source — spawnEveningAgent() under its own EVE_CAP, never a share of laneCap or eastCap — open from sunDown − 0.5 h to sunDown + 3 h when warmth is high, it is not raining, wetF() is low and windF() is below a stroll threshold; closed in winter. They enter by the park gate or the quay head, cross the FOOTBRIDGE (DECK_LEAD_A/Q, the #73 routes), lean at the rail (a.nightRail exists as ONE stander — widen it or give the deck its own lean spots), sit on the quay/far benches, and leave the way they came or via goHome/claimHome before the window's end (price with pathHours() against the END, the #53 law). Arrivals in twos via withCompanion. Count at the choice over 10 seeds × 4 days: arrivals per evening, presence by hour on the deck/quay/far bank, and the winter evening unchanged. An 80–150-line diff is expected.
successLooksLike: Tap the clock on a summer day and land at sunDown + 1 h with 4–8 people out on the quay, the deck and the far bank — some in pairs, some leaning at the rail over the river lights — and by sunDown + 3.5 h they have gone. A winter or a wet evening looks as it does today.
avoid: Not a share of an existing cap (the law: a rare thing needs its own source). Do not put them on the lane — the lane's evening is the tap door. Do not size the source by rate; size it by the places its walk reaches before the window ends.
